As an European living in the US, I agree with you that the US has stronger free speech laws than the EU (especially when you consider the hate speech denial laws, the right to be forgotten, and other stuff like that). Europe had her good share of trouble with speech (especially Germany, Italy, or Spain) and regulating hate speech has become part of the culture there.

Remember that free speech in the US only applies to government actions. Private companies and private individuals can still regulate speech as they see fit on their private property. A restaurant can decide not to post a flier with racist comments in its public bulletin board. A newspaper/tv station can decided not to run an ad that it finds distasteful. A website can decide to remove content accessible to the public that it deems unsafe for other users.

The difference between the US and Europe is that the US government cannot interfere with its citizens' speech. So it comes down to the single show owner/private citizen to limit speech on its property rather than the government limiting speech through court orders (as it often happens in Europe).
